Question Choices: Nine musicians audition for the distinct roles of soloist and accompanist. How many assignments are possible? Input C(... ...) and P(... ...) for combination and permutation.
Hints: The two roles are different;Choose the soloist and then the accompanist
Solution: Because the roles are distinct, the count is $P(9,2)=9\cdot8=72$.

Question Choices: Ten different books are available for four labeled display positions. How many displays can be made without repeating a book? Input C(... ...) and P(... ...) for combination and permutation.
Hints: The four display positions are distinct;Use four descending factors starting at 10
Solution: The display is an ordered selection, so $P(10,4)=10\cdot9\cdot8\cdot7=5040$.

Question Choices: Eight runners compete for first, second, third, and fourth place. How many ordered results are possible? Input C(... ...) and P(... ...) for combination and permutation.
Hints: The four finishing places are different;Use an ordered selection of 4 runners
Solution: Because the finishing places are distinct, the count is $P(8,4)=8\cdot7\cdot6\cdot5=1680$.

Question Choices: Eight runners compete, but only the set of four finalists matters. How many sets of finalists are possible? Input C(... ...) and P(... ...) for combination and permutation.
Hints: Start with the 1680 ordered results;Each set of four finalists appears in 4! orders;Divide by 24
Solution: There are $P(8,4)=1680$ ordered results.;Each set appears $4!=24$ times, so there are $1680/24=70$ sets.
